heroSub: 10 hand-picked stays around Khao Takiab, Hua Hin that we've already reviewed in depth — from a luxury Thai-colonial resort on the sand and bungalows tucked into a frangipani garden by the sea, to a quiet little private boutique and budget rooms near Cicada Market. Starting around ฿700–3,500/night.
heroStats: ✅ Honest takes from real reviews at every stay
introH2: 🏖️ What kinds of stays does Khao Takiab have, and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: Khao Takiab is a beach at the southern end of Hua Hin that many people choose because it's quieter and more private than the beaches in the town center. There's a hill and Wat Khao Takiab with full sea views, and it's close to Cicada Market and Tamarind Market, two popular spots for food and craft stalls · But "a beachfront stay at Khao Takiab" doesn't mean just one thing — some are 5-star Thai-colonial resorts that look like an old palace, some are small bungalows hidden in a frangipani garden with a private beach, some are quiet adults-only boutiques, and some are budget rooms starting in the low hundreds that you use as a base for getting out and about · Plenty of people book and end up with a vibe or location that doesn't match their kind of trip, and feel it wasn't worth it · This article rounds up 10 stays around Khao Takiab that we've already reviewed in depth, kept in the same order as the original popular list — every one comes from reading real guest reviews, with both the good points and the honest caveats, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Hua Hin has no rail transit · The Khao Takiab area sits about 6–8 km south of Hua Hin town, and the easiest way around is by private car, Grab, or a rented motorbike · From Bangkok it's about a 3-hour drive down the Phetkasem road, or take a van/train to Hua Hin and continue from there · Reference points in the area: Khao Takiab–Nong Kae beach, a quiet beach to the south that's more private than the town center · Wat Khao Takiab, with a large Buddha image, a sea viewpoint and a troop of monkeys to watch out for · Cicada Market and Tamarind Market, popular weekend craft-and-food markets · Reaching Hua Hin town, the train station and the night market takes about 10–20 min by car.

toc.name: Wora Bura Hua Hin Resort & Spa

entries.name: Wora Bura Hua Hin Resort & Spa
entries.badge: 🏛️ Most luxurious in the area · beachfront
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiab–Nong Kae · on the beach · 10–15 min walk to Cicada Market
tags: 🏛️ Thai-colonial architecture from the Rama V era
entries.addr: 83/199 Nong Kae, Khao Takiab area, Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
entries.storyHtml: If there's one stay on this list that stops you to take photos the moment you walk in, plenty of reviews give it to this one — Wora Bura Hua Hin Resort & Spa is a luxury 5-star resort on Khao Takiab–Nong Kae beach, designed throughout as cream-white buildings in a Thai-colonial style, inspired by the era when King Rama V toured Europe and drawing on Mrigadayavan Palace, Vimanmek Mansion and Ban Puen Palace · What makes people fall for it is that it has only 77 rooms and villas, named after Thai provinces, so it never feels crowded, and even the entry-level rooms are a generous 44 sqm — wider than the standard rooms at many resorts in the same area · The highlight reviews mention most is the free-form beachfront pool with a jacuzzi facing the Gulf of Thailand, so you can swim and look out to sea at the same time, paired with the Wora Spa, a gym, a library and a Kids Club for families · Real reviews praise the service most — staff are warm and helpful from check-in, the service score on Trip.com runs as high as around 9.3, and breakfast gets credit for variety across both Thai and Western dishes · The location is an advantage too, since it's about a 10–15 min walk to Cicada Market and Tamarind Market with their many food stalls · The honest caveats from the reviews: the resort leans into a classic, period style, so some in-room items and details are starting to show their age, water pressure in some bathrooms is weak, the dinner dining options within the resort are limited and some drinks are pricey, and the walk to the night market is fairly dark late at night · This isn't the cheapest stay in the area, but it's the most luxurious and the most distinctive on design — well suited to couples who want a romantic atmosphere, families after a quiet beachfront resort with a Kids Club, and anyone tired of high-rise resorts who wants a place with a story.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Many entry-level rooms are garden view, so if you want a sea or pool view, request it when you book · If you're coming to swim, plan around the beachfront pool since the beach depends on the tide (pool open 07:00–19:00) · For dinner, walking to Cicada/Tamarind Market gives you more food choices and is cheaper.
pros: Distinctive Thai-colonial architecture, photogenic from every angle
Entry rooms are 44 sqm, larger than the price suggests · only 77 rooms, never crowded
Beachfront pool with sea views + a full Kids Club and spa, great for families
Service is consistently praised, Trip.com service score around 9.3 (from reviews)
cons: Classic-style resort, some details starting to age, water pressure weak in some rooms
Limited dinner dining options within the resort, some drinks are pricey
Beach depends on the tide, and the walk to the night market is fairly dark late at night (from reviews)

entries.type: Boutique beachfront resort 4-star · on a private beach
entries.name: Supatra Hua Hin Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiab–Nong Kae · on a private beach · 600–700 m walk to Wat Khao Takiab
entries.addr: 143/18 Takiab Road, Nong Kae, Khao Takiab, Hua Hin
entries.storyHtml: Supatra Hua Hin Resort is a small beachfront resort of about 18 rooms sitting at the far end of the Khao Takiab area, and what people talk about most is that it has a private beach right out front — a few steps from your room down to the sea, which is hard to find at this price · Instead of a high-rise hotel, this is small bungalows and cabanas decorated in a contemporary Thai style, scattered and tucked into a shady garden under frangipani trees, and many reviews say it feels more like staying at a friend's holiday house than checking into a hotel · Another highlight is the outdoor pool that looks out to the sea and the sand, ringed by a tropical garden, paired with an open-air seaside café with good views where you can sit comfortably all day · A hard-to-find selling point is the pet-friendly policy — many dog and cat owners choose this place so they can bring their pets to the beach together, and the staff get credit for being warm and friendly, with the close attention you get at a small stay · The honest caveats from the reviews: this is a resort where the building is getting on in years, so the rooms and some of the upkeep are starting to show their age, there's a bit of peeling paint, some rooms are fairly dark because of the dark-toned wood, and importantly, Khao Takiab has a troop of wild monkeys that often come into the grounds in the morning, so keep food and belongings well secured · Breakfast has few options and the area is fairly far from walkable restaurants, so if you don't have a car, plan to call a ride · Best suited to couples wanting quiet romance, small families who want their kids to play on the beach right out front, and people bringing pets — set your expectations around charm and location rather than how new the rooms are.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The monkeys are real — shut doors and windows tight and don't leave food or bags on the balcony · If you're sensitive to wear and tear or want a sea view, ask for a higher-grade or recently renovated room and check the latest photos before booking · Ask about the status of the pool and any renovation work before you travel, and if you're bringing a pet, give advance notice.
pros: Private beach out front, you can walk straight into the sea, quiet with few people
Bungalows in a shady frangipani garden, a pool with sea views, a café with good views on the beach
Pet-friendly, you can bring dogs and cats to the beach — a rare selling point at this price
Warm, friendly staff with close attention as at a small stay (from reviews)
cons: Building is getting on in years, rooms and some upkeep starting to age, some rooms fairly dark
Monkeys come around in the morning, so keep food and belongings well secured
Few breakfast options, and the area is fairly far from walkable restaurants (from reviews)

entries.name: Baan Sabaaidee
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiab–Nong Kae · on a soi · walkable to the beach
entries.addr: Khao Takiab area, Nong Kae, Hua Hin (on a soi, walkable to the beach)
entries.storyHtml: Baan Sabaaidee is a small boutique of about 18 studios that sells exactly what many people are after on a relaxing trip — quiet, calm and adults-only privacy — because the resort takes adult guests only, with no kids running around, making it a favourite of couples and people on honeymoon or who simply want a real rest · What reviews agree on is the lovely, shady garden with a saltwater pool in the middle that doesn't sting your eyes, very clean studios, comfortable beds, good-quality linens, and importantly, it's well maintained and not left to fall into disrepair · The cleanliness score on Booking.com runs as high as around 9.2, which is very high for a stay at this level · Many of the studio types have a microwave, fridge and kettle built in, making them handy for anyone wanting a longer stay or to cook simple meals · The owner and staff also get credit for being warm and friendly, and there's free parking · Reviews say the location is walkable to Khao Takiab beach and close to Wat Khao Takiab, but you do need to understand honestly that the stay is on a soi, not on the beach and not on a main road, so without your own car, plan to use Grab · Other notes from the reviews: there's no all-day restaurant, so check on breakfast before booking, there's no gym or full spa in the small-boutique style, and with few rooms it fills up fast in high season · Best suited to couples and people who value quiet, cleanliness and privacy over the full set of amenities you'd get at a big resort.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: This place is adults only, so if you're travelling with kids, pick another stay on this list instead · The stay is on a soi, not on the beach, so have a car or Grab ready · There's no all-day restaurant, so check breakfast terms before booking, and with few rooms, book ahead in high season.
pros: Quiet and private as it's adults only, great for couples and honeymooners
Lovely shady garden, saltwater pool in the garden, very clean rooms (cleanliness score around 9.2)
Studios with microwave, fridge and kettle, handy for longer stays
Warm, friendly owner and staff, free parking (from reviews)
cons: On a soi, not on the beach or a main road, so you need a car or Grab
No kids · no all-day restaurant, so check breakfast before booking
No gym/spa, and with about 18 rooms it fills up fast in high season (from reviews)

entries.type: Budget boutique hotel 3-star · next to Cicada Market
entries.name: NornDee Hotel Hua Hin
entries.badge: 🛍️ Next to Cicada Market · great value
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiab–Nong Kae · next to Cicada Market · walkable to the beach
entries.addr: Nong Kae–Khao Takiab Road, next to Cicada Market, Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
entries.storyHtml: NornDee Hotel Hua Hin is a budget boutique hotel of about 30 rooms that has been open since 2015, and its clearest selling point is its location right next to Cicada Market, one of Hua Hin's popular craft-and-food markets — walk out of the stay and you're at the food stalls, and it's walkable to Khao Takiab beach · It suits people who want to explore the Khao Takiab area on a budget but still want a clean, cute room rather than a run-down one · Reviews agree the rooms have cute boutique decor, comfortable beds, friendly and helpful staff, a 24-hour front desk, and an on-site café where guests get a discount, plus a small garden pool for a cooling dip · There's free private parking, and it's close to the seafood restaurants and well-known cafés of the Nong Kae area, so it suits couples, small families and groups driving in themselves · The honest caveats from the reviews: it's a building that's been open since 2015, so some rooms with lots of wood have a musty, damp smell in the rainy season, and some towels and items are starting to age, and the stay isn't directly on the beach so you have to walk or take a short ride · Breakfast is simple with few options for buffet lovers, on nights the market is open you may hear music or activity, and the small pool isn't for serious lap swimming · Overall a good-value pick for people who value a location next to food and cute rooms over luxury.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The strength here is being walkable to Cicada Market, so coming on a weekend when the market is open makes the most of the location · If you're sensitive to noise, ask for a room not facing the market side on activity nights · The stay isn't directly on the beach, so allow time for a walk or a short ride down to the sand.
pros: Location next to Cicada Market, walkable to food and to the beach
Clean rooms with cute boutique decor and comfortable beds
On-site café with a guest discount, a small garden pool, a 24-hr front desk
Friendly staff, free private parking, good value for the price (from reviews)
cons: Building open since 2015, some rooms with lots of wood have a musty, damp smell in the rainy season
Not directly on the beach, so you have to walk or take a short ride
Breakfast is simple with few options, on market nights you may hear activity (from reviews)

entries.name: The Bihai Hua Hin
entries.badge: 🏆 Highest score in the area · quiet and private
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiab–Nong Kae · ~140 m walk to the beach
tags: 🏆 Highest overall score on the list, 9.4
🏊 Two pools, including a rooftop infinity pool
🛏️ Spacious 44–52 sqm rooms, balcony in every room
entries.addr: Khao Takiab area, Nong Kae, Hua Hin (~140 m walk to the beach)
entries.storyHtml: On this list, measured on overall score alone, The Bihai Hua Hin is the highest at 9.4 — a small boutique resort of just 15 rooms selling quiet privacy on Khao Takiab beach, only about 140 m from the sand · What pushes the score up is room quality and service — rooms are a generous 44–52 sqm, every one has a balcony, they're very clean, the cleanliness score on the review platforms runs as high as around 9.6 and the service score as high as around 9.7, which is very high even compared with big resorts · The highlight reviews mention often is the two pools, including a rooftop infinity pool with a wide view, paired with a private tropical garden that's warm and inviting to relax in, and breakfast that many say is tasty and better presented than expected for a small stay · The overall feel is private, suited to couples and small families wanting calm · The honest caveats from the reviews: some of the actual rooms may not match the booking-site photos from every angle, restaurants around the Khao Takiab area are fairly pricey, the resort sits on a small soi that drivers may find hard to find the first time, there's no gym or full spa as at a big resort, and it's about 10–15 min by car from Hua Hin town and the night market · And with only 15 rooms it fills up fast in high season · Best suited to people after a small, high-scoring stay with spacious clean rooms and close service, rather than those wanting the full set of big-resort amenities or a spot right on the sand and in the town center.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only 15 rooms and a high score, book ahead in high season as it fills up fast · If you want easy pool access, choose a Pool Access room where you can step straight into the pool · Set your map navigation carefully since it's on a small soi, and budget for meals as restaurants around the area are fairly pricey.
pros: Highest overall score on the list, 9.4 · cleanliness and service as high as around 9.6–9.7
Spacious 44–52 sqm rooms with a balcony in every room, quiet and private at just 15 rooms
Two pools, including a rooftop infinity pool with a wide view, a warm garden
Breakfast praised as better presented than expected for a small stay (from reviews)
cons: Some actual rooms may not match the booking-site photos from every angle · no gym/full spa
On a small soi, hard to find the first time · restaurants around the area are fairly pricey
Only 15 rooms, fills up fast in high season · about 10–15 min by car from the town center (from reviews)

entries.type: Small resort 3-star · with a pool and slide
entries.name: Milano Huahin
entries.badge: 🛝 Pool with a slide · budget families
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiab · Soi Hua Hin 114 · near Cicada Market and Vana Nava
tags: 🛝 Pool with a slide and a kids' pool
entries.addr: Soi Hua Hin 114, Khao Takiab area, Hua Hin
entries.storyHtml: Milano Huahin is a small resort of about 34 rooms on Soi Hua Hin 114 in the Khao Takiab area, and its clearest selling point is a pool with a kids' pool and a slide at prices starting in just the low hundreds, which is why many budget families choose it — the kids can play on the slide without paying a lot · The setting is a quiet garden on a soi, parking is easy, and many reviews say the beds are soft and comfortable and the staff are friendly · The location works too, since it's near Cicada Market, Tamarind Market and the Vana Nava water park, all popular spots, and there's a local shuttle for people who don't drive in · The Pool Access rooms are also a convenient walk to the pool, good for families · It has to be said this is a budget stay, so the reviews do flag some upkeep notes — some bathrooms have a smell from the drain, some bathroom fittings are starting to age or break, power outlets in the room are limited (a power strip is recommended), the Wi-Fi signal isn't strong in some spots, the fridge in some rooms cuts off when you leave, and booking communication is sometimes not smooth · These are things to accept for the price rather than big problems · Best suited to budget families and couples who want a pool and slide at an easy price and to use the stay as a base for getting out around Khao Takiab.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The selling point is the pool with a slide, so if you're travelling with kids, choose a Pool Access room for an easy walk to the pool · Bring your own power strip since outlets in the room are limited · If you don't drive in, ask about the resort's local shuttle, and compare prices across 3 sites as they move with the season.
pros: Pool with a kids' pool and a slide, great for families, at prices from the low hundreds
Quiet garden setting on a soi, easy parking, soft and comfortable beds
Near Cicada Market, Tamarind Market and Vana Nava · local shuttle available
Good value given it has a pool and slide (from reviews)
cons: Some bathrooms have a smell from the drain, some fittings starting to age/break
Limited power outlets in the room · Wi-Fi not strong in some spots · fridge cuts off in some rooms
Booking communication is sometimes not smooth (from reviews)

entries.type: Beachfront hotel 4-star · on the southern Hua Hin beach
entries.name: Chom View Hotel, Hua Hin
entries.badge: 🏖️ On the beach · two pools with a slide
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nong Kae–Khao Takiab · on the beach · south of town, walkable to Cicada Market
tags: 🏖️ On the southern Hua Hin beach
🛝 Two pools with a slide and a kids' pool
🏠 Family Duplex ~100 sqm with a kitchen
🍜 Walkable to Cicada and Tamarind Markets
entries.addr: Southern Hua Hin beach, Nong Kae–Khao Takiab, Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
entries.storyHtml: Chom View Hotel, Hua Hin is a 134-room beachfront hotel on the southern Hua Hin beach in the Nong Kae–Khao Takiab area, and its clearest selling point is a location right on the beach where you can walk straight into the sea, in a zone that's quieter than central Hua Hin, suited to families who want their kids to play in the sand and water right in front of the hotel · There are two pools with a slide and a kids' pool that kids love, and it's a walkable distance to Cicada and Tamarind Markets for food · What reviews praise especially is the Family Duplex of about 100 sqm that's very spacious and fully equipped with a fridge, microwave and kitchen items, good for large families or groups, as well as the sea-view Ocean View Duplex at a price that's good value given you're staying on the beach · There's also Thai massage on the beach and a seaside bar with a nice atmosphere · It has to be said honestly that the score here isn't as high as some places on the list, because the reviews reflect that the building and some rooms are starting to age and the details aren't yet polished, cleanliness in some rooms still needs work, and staff service and communication are sometimes inconsistent, with room cleaning or check-out occasionally slow · Breakfast options are ordinary, and you should check first whether the price includes breakfast · Best suited to families who want a large room on the beach at good value, setting expectations around location and room space rather than how new and polished the service is.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're travelling as a group, the Family Duplex (~100 sqm) with a full kitchen is the best-value choice · If you're coming to swim, plan around the two pools with the slide · Check before booking whether the price includes breakfast, and compare 3 sites as high-season prices climb fast.
pros: Location on the beach, you can walk straight into the sea, quieter than central Hua Hin
Two pools with a slide and a kids' pool, great for families, walkable to Cicada Market
Family Duplex ~100 sqm is very spacious with a full kitchen · sea-view rooms available
Thai massage on the beach and a seaside bar with a nice atmosphere, easy on the budget (from reviews)
cons: The building and some rooms are starting to age, details not yet polished
Cleanliness in some rooms and service/communication are sometimes inconsistent
Breakfast options are ordinary, check whether breakfast is included (from reviews)

entries.type: Serviced apartment 3-star · suites with a kitchen
entries.name: First Choice Grand Suites
entries.badge: 🍳 Suites with a kitchen · great for long stays
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiab–Nong Kae · on a soi · ~4 min walk to the beach
tags: 🍳 Suites with a built-in kitchen, large fridge
🌸 Pool ringed by frangipani, with a kids' pool
🚗 ~4 min walk to the beach · free parking
entries.addr: Khao Takiab area, Nong Kae, Hua Hin (on a soi, ~4 min walk to the beach)
entries.storyHtml: First Choice Grand Suites is a serviced apartment of about 17 suites in the Khao Takiab area, and its clearest selling point is condo-sized suites with a built-in kitchen including a large fridge and a stove, so you can cook for yourself — great for people wanting a longer stay or families wanting to save on food · Reviews agree the rooms are very clean and quiet, the cleanliness score on the platforms runs as high as around 9.0, and there's a pool ringed by frangipani trees that's pretty and clean with a kids' pool · Many room types have a separate bedroom and a sitting area, a private balcony looking out to mountains, the sea or the golf course, and it's a few minutes' walk to Khao Takiab beach (about 4 min), with free parking · It's near Cicada Market, Khao Takiab and the seafood restaurants, so it's especially good value for a longer stay and for families · The honest caveats from the reviews: the location is deep on a soi, inconvenient to get around without your own car, there's no on-site restaurant or shop and no 24-hour front desk, service can be slow as there are few staff, English communication is a bit limited for foreigners, and the Wi-Fi signal varies from room to room · This isn't a full-service stay or one with a spa like a big resort · Best suited to people who value a spacious room with a kitchen, quiet, and value for a longer stay over full-service amenities and a location in the middle of the buzz.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The selling point is the in-room kitchen, so for a longer stay or a group, the Two-Bedroom Suite is the best value · The location is deep on a soi, so have your own car or Grab ready · There's no on-site shop and no 24-hr front desk, so plan to stock up on food to keep in the room.
pros: Spacious suites with a built-in kitchen and a large fridge, you can cook for yourself, great for long stays
Very clean and quiet (cleanliness score around 9.0) · pool ringed by frangipani with a kids' pool
Separate bedroom + sitting area, balcony with mountain/sea/golf-course views
~4 min walk to the beach, free parking, near Cicada Market (from reviews)
cons: Location deep on a soi, inconvenient to get around without your own car
No on-site restaurant/shop and no 24-hour front desk
Service can be slow as there are few staff · Wi-Fi varies from room to room (from reviews)

entries.type: Small budget boutique stay · near Cicada Market
entries.name: Stone Head Hua Hin
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiab · Soi Hua Hin 106 · walkable to Cicada Market
entries.addr: Soi Hua Hin 106, Khao Takiab area, Hua Hin (near Cicada Market)
entries.storyHtml: Stone Head Hua Hin is a small boutique stay of about 26 rooms that's the cheapest option on this list, with prices from just ฿700, but what people like is that it doesn't drop its standards of cleanliness and quiet to match the price · Real reviews agree the rooms are clean, the beds are comfortable, the decor is simple, modern and clean-looking, and it's on a quiet soi where you sleep well with no disturbance · The owner and staff are friendly, helping recommend restaurants and places to visit, there are free bikes and free parking, and it's walkable to Cicada Market and near Bluport and Market Village, so it's good for using the room as a base for getting out · Many reviews also say it's safe, suited to solo travellers and women travelling alone · But it has to be made clear honestly that at this price the place has no swimming pool, isn't on the beach, and has no lift, so if you stay on an upper floor you have to carry your bags up the stairs, and breakfast is very simple (toast, tea, coffee) · Other notes from the reviews: some room types are compact, the internet is slow at times, and some found the damage deposit fairly high · Best suited to people who genuinely want to visit Hua Hin on a budget without dropping standards of cleanliness and quiet, and who are ready to head out to find the beach and food themselves, rather than those who want a pool and a spot right on the sand.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: This place isn't on the beach and has no pool, so use the stay's free bikes to ride to the beach and Cicada Market · There's no lift, so if you'd rather not carry bags up the stairs, ask for a ground-floor room · Check the damage-deposit terms at check-in in advance.
pros: From ฿700, cheapest on the list, but the rooms are clean with comfortable beds
Quiet soi for good sleep · free bikes and free parking, walkable to Cicada Market
Friendly owner and staff who help recommend restaurants and places to visit
Safe, suited to solo travellers and women travelling alone (from reviews)
cons: No swimming pool, not on the beach, and no lift (upper floors mean carrying bags up the stairs)
Breakfast is very simple · some room types are compact
Internet slow at times · some found the damage deposit high (from reviews)

entries.type: Small resort 4-star · rooms with a kitchen, near the beach
entries.name: Surf and Sand Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khao Takiab–Nong Kae · near the beach and Wat Khao Takiab
tags: 🍳 Rooms with a built-in kitchen, you can cook for yourself
🏊 Pool with a jacuzzi and a kids' pool
entries.addr: Khao Takiab area, Nong Kae, Hua Hin (near Wat Khao Takiab and the beach)
entries.storyHtml: Closing the list is Surf and Sand Resort, a small resort of about 22 units in the Khao Takiab area with the most reviews on this list (around 309 reviews), and its clearest selling point is spacious rooms with a built-in kitchen where you can cook for yourself, paired with service that's attentive like family · Reviews say it's especially good value for a longer stay and for groups, since the studios connect into two bedrooms, good for families and groups of friends, and many rooms have a balcony looking onto the pool · There's a pool with a jacuzzi and a kids' pool that's kept clean, the location is an easy walk to Khao Takiab beach and Wat Khao Takiab, and a hard-to-find feature is that it's pet-friendly · The owner and staff get credit for being warm and friendly, and some help arrange golf rounds and recommend places to visit · The honest caveats from the reviews: it's a small resort, so some furniture and decor are starting to age, the team is small so at busy times you may wait, breakfast options are fairly few and simple, it doesn't have the full set of amenities of a big resort, it's not directly on the beach so you cross a small road, and prices at some times feel high compared with nearby stays · Best suited to people who want a small, warm resort with a spacious room and a kitchen, near the beach, where pets are welcome, and coming as a group for a longer stay, rather than those after the full set of amenities and a brand-new room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The selling point is the in-room kitchen, so for a longer stay or a group, choosing the connecting studios is the best value · If you're bringing a pet, give notice and confirm the terms in advance · It's not directly on the beach, so allow time for a short walk across the road down to the sand, and compare prices across 3 sites before booking.
pros: Spacious rooms with a built-in kitchen, you can cook for yourself, especially good value for long stays
Connecting studios, good for families and groups of friends
Pool with a jacuzzi and a kids' pool, near the beach and Wat Khao Takiab · pet-friendly
Warm owner and staff who help arrange golf rounds and recommend places to visit (from reviews)
cons: Small resort, some furniture and decor starting to age, small team so you may wait at busy times
Breakfast options fairly few · doesn't have the full amenities of a big resort
Not directly on the beach, you cross a small road · prices at some times feel high (from reviews)

adviceTitle: How do you pick the right Khao Takiab beach stay for your trip?

advice.head: Want a distinctive luxury beachfront resort
advice.bodyHtml: → Wora Bura Hua Hin Resort & Spa ฿3,500, a 5-star Thai-colonial resort on the beach, sea-view pool, Kids Club, just 77 rooms, score 9.1

advice.head: Want to stay on a private beach, holiday-house style
advice.bodyHtml: → Supatra Hua Hin Resort ฿1,900, bungalows in a frangipani garden on a private beach, a pool with sea views, pet-friendly · or Chom View ฿1,500, on the beach with two pools and a slide

advice.head: A couples' trip, you want quiet privacy
advice.bodyHtml: → Baan Sabaaidee ฿1,500, an adults-only boutique, saltwater pool in the garden, high cleanliness · or The Bihai Hua Hin ฿1,800, a small 15-room boutique, highest score at 9.4

advice.head: Long stay, coming as a group, want an in-room kitchen
advice.bodyHtml: → First Choice Grand Suites ฿1,300, condo-sized suites with a kitchen · or Surf and Sand Resort ฿1,100, rooms with a kitchen that connect, pet-friendly

advice.head: A family with kids, you want a fun pool
advice.bodyHtml: → Milano Huahin ฿900, a pool with a slide at an easy price · or Chom View ฿1,500, on the beach with two pools and a slide, Family Duplex ~100 sqm

advice.head: Want to visit Khao Takiab on a budget
advice.bodyHtml: → Stone Head Hua Hin ฿700, cheapest, clean rooms, free bikes, walkable to Cicada Market · or NornDee Hotel ฿1,200, next to Cicada Market, cute boutique rooms

advice.head: Want to be walkable to Cicada Market and food
advice.bodyHtml: → NornDee Hotel ฿1,200, next to Cicada Market with an on-site café · or Stone Head ฿700, walkable to Cicada Market, Bluport and Market Village

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates from the standard-room range and may change by date and season — we recommend checking real prices and comparing 3 sites before every booking · The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms, not from staying ourselves · The order in the list is carried over from the original popular list, following the same positions for all 10 stays, not a re-ranking by score · The Khao Takiab area has a troop of wild monkeys, especially around Wat Khao Takiab, so keep food and belongings well secured · The Gulf of Thailand beaches depend on the tide, so many stays rely mainly on the pool · During high season (November–February) and long holidays, Hua Hin fills up fast and prices climb, so book ahead and choose free cancellation if your plans aren't firm · Hua Hin has no rail transit, so a private car, Grab or a rented motorbike is the most convenient way around the Khao Takiab area · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Khao Takiab beach stays in Hua Hin

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best Khao Takiab beach stay?
faq.a: It depends on your style of trip and budget · If you want a distinctive luxury beachfront resort, Wora Bura Hua Hin Resort & Spa is a 5-star Thai-colonial place on the beach, score 9.1 · Measured on overall score alone, The Bihai Hua Hin is the highest on the list at 9.4 (a small 15-room boutique) · If you want to stay on a private beach and can bring pets, Supatra Hua Hin Resort · For a couple wanting quiet, Baan Sabaaidee (adults only) · And on a budget, Stone Head Hua Hin from ฿700

faq.q: ❓ How much do Khao Takiab stays cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at around ฿700–3,500 per night · The most budget-friendly are Stone Head from ฿700 and Milano from ฿900 · Mid-range are Surf and Sand ฿1,100, NornDee ฿1,200, First Choice Grand Suites ฿1,300, Chom View and Baan Sabaaidee ฿1,500, The Bihai ฿1,800, Supatra ฿1,900 · And the most luxurious is Wora Bura from ฿3,500 · All prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms, and during festivals and on Saturdays prices may be higher than usual

faq.q: ❓ Which Khao Takiab stays are really on the beach?
faq.a: The ones on the beach or with a private beach out front are Wora Bura (on Nong Kae–Khao Takiab beach), Supatra (private beach out front) and Chom View (on the southern Hua Hin beach) · Those a few minutes' walk to the beach are The Bihai (~140 m), First Choice Grand Suites (~4 min), Baan Sabaaidee and Surf and Sand · As for NornDee, Milano and Stone Head, they're on a soi away from the beach, so you have to walk or take a short ride · Note: the Gulf of Thailand beaches depend on the tide, so many stays rely mainly on the pool

faq.q: ❓ Does Khao Takiab really have monkeys, and what do I watch out for?
faq.a: Yes · The Khao Takiab area, especially around Wat Khao Takiab, is home to a troop of wild monkeys that often come into the grounds of stays in the morning · You should shut doors and windows tight and not leave food or bags on the balcony, and be careful carrying food when walking around the stay · If you know about it in advance, it's manageable with no problem, and not every stay encounters monkeys as often — those near the foot of the hill and the temple see them more often

faq.q: ❓ Which Khao Takiab stays are good for families with kids?
faq.a: The best for families with kids are the ones with a fun pool and large rooms · Milano Huahin ฿900 has a kids' pool and a slide at an easy price · Chom View ฿1,500 is on the beach with two pools and a slide, and a Family Duplex ~100 sqm · Wora Bura has a Kids Club and a beachfront pool · And First Choice Grand Suites and Surf and Sand Resort have rooms with a kitchen, good for families who want to cook for themselves and stay longer · Note: Baan Sabaaidee is adults only and not suited to kids

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Khao Takiab stay?
faq.a: Many stays in the Khao Takiab area are small (some just 15–18 rooms), so they fill up fast · During high season (November–February), long holidays and on Saturdays, book 3–4 weeks or more ahead, especially The Bihai, Baan Sabaaidee and Supatra, which have few rooms · In the normal season, 1–2 weeks is enough · Every platform usually has Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in that kind of rate if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price
